implementation_notes: When the reply is a protobuf message the mask is the canonical contract: accept it as a system parameter (fields=user.displayName,photo) or gRPC metadata, parse it with util::FieldMaskUtil::FromJsonString, and validate it against the descriptor with IsValidFieldMask<T>() before doing any work. The projection itself is util::FieldMaskUtil::TrimMessage(mask, &message), which removes every field not represented in the mask (an empty mask means 'do nothing'); ToCanonicalForm/Union/Intersect/Subtract cover merged masks, and TrimOptions::keep_required_fields preserves proto2 required fields. Hand-written structs skip the util and project inside their own writer.
pitfalls: An empty mask is a no-op in FieldMaskUtil, so an absent selector must be expanded to the default view explicitly instead of being passed through as an empty mask.

The proto name (snake_case) and the JSON name (lowerCamelCase) are different spellings of the same path; FromString versus FromJsonString pick different conventions and mixing them makes valid paths look unmappable.
TrimMessage mutates the message in place - copy before trimming if the instance is shared with a cache or another caller.

variants.name: Generic JSON document projection with nlohmann::json::erase
variants.idiom_name: nlohmann::json erase loop over the allowlist
variants.implementation_notes: Document-style servers that already hold the reply as a generic JSON value project it after the fact: walk the object and erase every key that the caller did not name (basic_json::erase(key), or the iterator form to erase more than one key safely). Nested selections recurse into sub-objects. This is the cheapest way to bolt partial responses onto an existing generic pipeline, at the price of materializing and then discarding data.
pitfalls: erase() invalidates iterators at and after the erased element - use the returned iterator, never ++it after erasing.
Projection runs after the whole document was built, so CPU and allocation stay at full-resource cost; do not present it as a performance win on hot paths.
Key comparison is byte-wise: request names in a different case or spelling (camelCase vs snake_case) silently erase everything.
